convention: Planetocentric latitude (north positive) and east-positive longitude in [-180, 180), Moon Mean Earth/Polar Axis frame (DE421 cartographic, as used by LOLA and LROC).

databook.label: NASA Lunar Surface Data Book, ACD-50044 Rev A (2023), Table A2-2

nssdc.label: NASA NSSDC, Apollo Landing Sites (LRO-measured LM positions)

lroc-im2.label: LROC: IM-2 landing region (intended site on Mons Mouton)

lroc-bg1.label: LROC: Firefly Blue Ghost landing region, 18.56°N 61.81°E

sites.name: Shackleton Rim
sites.blurb: Ridge on Shackleton crater's rim, a few kilometres from the south pole. Among the best-lit terrain on the Moon.

sites.name: Connecting Ridge
sites.blurb: Ridge linking the rims of Shackleton and de Gerlache craters.

sites.name: Shackleton Rim B
sites.blurb: Shackleton's rim on the opposite side of the crater from R04.

sites.name: Peak Near Shackleton
sites.blurb: Isolated high peak about 40 km from the pole.

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim 1
sites.blurb: Raised rim of de Gerlache crater, Earth-facing side of the pole.

sites.name: de Gerlache–Kocher Massif
sites.blurb: Massif between de Gerlache and Kocher craters, on the far-side-facing hemisphere.

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.blurb: Five-kilometre-high massif near the prime meridian; long, Earth-facing views.

sites.name: Leibnitz Beta Plateau
sites.blurb: High plateau also called Mons Mouton, a NASA Artemis candidate region.

sites.name: Nobile Rim 1
sites.blurb: Rim of Nobile crater, beside the Leibnitz Beta plateau.

sites.name: Haworth
sites.blurb: Reference point at Haworth crater, a permanently shadowed crater on the near side.

sites.name: Cabeus Exterior Wall 1
sites.blurb: Outer wall of Cabeus, near the LCROSS impact crater.

sites.name: Amundsen Rim
sites.blurb: Rim of the 100-km Amundsen crater.

sites.name: Odysseus (IM-1)
sites.blurb: Intuitive Machines' Nova-C lander touched down near Malapert A on 22 Feb 2024.

sites.name: IM-2 target, Mons Mouton
sites.blurb: Intended IM-2 site on Mons Mouton. Athena landed nearby on 6 Mar 2025 but tipped over.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3
sites.blurb: ISRO's Vikram lander, 23 Aug 2023. It was the first landing at high southern latitude.

sites.name: Chang'e 4
sites.blurb: The first far-side landing, in Von Kármán crater, 3 Jan 2019. Earth is never visible from here; it relays via Queqiao.

sites.name: Blue Ghost M1
sites.blurb: Firefly's CLPS lander in Mare Crisium near Mons Latreille, 2 Mar 2025.

sites.name: Apollo 11
sites.blurb: Tranquility Base, Eagle LM, 20 Jul 1969.

sites.name: Apollo 12
sites.blurb: Ocean of Storms, beside Surveyor 3, 19 Nov 1969.

sites.name: Apollo 14
sites.blurb: Fra Mauro highlands, 5 Feb 1971.

sites.name: Apollo 15
sites.blurb: Hadley–Apennine, beside Hadley Rille, 30 Jul 1971.

sites.name: Apollo 16
sites.blurb: Descartes highlands, 21 Apr 1972.

sites.name: Apollo 17
sites.blurb: Taurus–Littrow valley, 11 Dec 1972.
